topic: Template Function Overloading with Operator Templates
explanation: In C++, operator overloading allows defining custom behaviors for operators when applied to user-defined types. When combined with templates, it enables generic operator implementations that work across various types, enhancing code reusability and type safety. This is particularly useful for container classes like std::multimap, where comparison operators can be templated to work with different key and value types, ensuring consistent behavior across diverse instantiations.
syntax:
template <class Key, class T, class Compare, class Allocator>
bool operator!=(const multimap<Key,T,Compare,Allocator>& x, const multimap<Key,T,Compare,Allocator>& y);
code_example: template <typename Key, typename T, typename Compare, typename Allocator>
bool operator!=(const std::multimap<Key, T, Compare, Allocator>& x, const std::multimap<Key, T, Compare, Allocator>& y) {
example_explanation: This example defines a template function that overloads the '!=' operator for std::multimap instances, allowing comparison of two multimaps regardless of their key, value, comparator, or allocator types. In main(), two multimaps are created with identical contents; the overloaded operator is used to compare them, demonstrating how templates facilitate generic operator overloading for standard library containers in modern C++.
